note: On another occasion Rabbi Yohanan came upon the young son of Reish Lakish, his late study partner, sitting and reciting a verse from Proverbs: a man's own foolishness ruins his path, and then his heart rages against God. Rabbi Yohanan wondered aloud whether this idea had any hint in the Torah itself. The boy answered at once with Genesis, where Joseph's brothers, in trouble, ask what God has done to them. Rabbi Yohanan raised his eyes and stared at him, and the boy's mother hurried him away, afraid Rabbi Yohanan would do to her son what he had done to his father.
why: It is a second tale about the same clever boy, following his exchange with Rabbi Yohanan about tithes; the Gemara then calls it a digression and returns to Rabbi Yohanan's teachings about rain.

people.name: Rabbi Yohanan
people.about: Leading Sage of the Land of Israel; Reish Lakish was his study partner and brother-in-law.

people.name: Reish Lakish
people.about: Rabbi Yohanan's great study partner, already dead here; the boy's father.

terms.meaning: The third part of the Hebrew Bible, after the Torah (the Five Books of Moses) and the Prophets. It includes Psalms, Proverbs, Job and other books.

note: Rav Daniel bar Ketina owned a garden and walked through it every day to see what it needed. He would say: this bed needs water, and this bed does not. Then rain would come and water exactly the places that needed it, and nowhere else.
why: The Gemara has just read a verse from Zechariah to mean that rain can fall for a single person, a single field, even a single plant; Rav Daniel's garden shows it happening.

people.name: Rav Daniel bar Ketina
people.about: A Babylonian Sage, remembered here for rain that fell only where his garden needed it.

note: Rabbi Abba the priest reported, in the name of Rabbi Yosei the priest, that the sons of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Hanina died, and that throughout the seven days of mourning he bathed in cold water.
why: Rava has ruled that a mourner may bathe in cold water, and this report is offered as support. The Gemara turns it aside: his periods of mourning came one right after another, a case where the rules are eased anyway.

people.name: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina
people.about: A Sage of the Land of Israel whose sons died; the report concerns how he mourned them.

people.name: Rabbi Abba the priest
people.about: The Sage who passes the report on.

people.name: Rabbi Yosei the priest
people.about: The Sage in whose name the report is given.

terms.meaning: After a close relative dies, Jewish law sets a week of intense mourning (shiva) with restrictions on bathing, grooming and pleasures.
